steps.message: Reviewing the intake for Great Kills Branch Library (fictional).

claims.text: Rooftop solar of about 41.7 kW covers about 20.8% of 240,000 kWh annual use, so solar alone does not reach the 30% goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Capital budget USD 350,000 (2026) from intake.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency first, then solar within budget; only the full path with a battery reaches the goal at the low end.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: 15,000 sq ft library built in 1985, flat roof of 5,000 sq ft, in Staten Island.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Public records match the intake for floor area and year built.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: System losses of 10-18% around the PVWatts default of 14% give the low and high output.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Usable roof fraction 0.55 for setbacks and mechanical zones.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: About 66 sq ft per kW for a flat commercial array layout.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10-20% of annual use, from published benchmarks, not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Planning-level benchmark prices, not quotes: solar $3,000-4,500/kW DC, battery $600-1,000/kWh, standard efficiency $4-8/sq ft saving 10-20%, deep efficiency $10-16/sq ft saving 15-25%; usable battery share 85%-100%; the 30% federal credit counts only when the incentives tool says the program is open.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Baseline is 240,000 kWh/yr from twelve months of bills.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Start with LED lighting and controls; savings use benchmark percentages until a building model exists.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: C1 usable roof about 2,750 sq ft (5,000 x 0.55).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: C2 array about 41.7 kW DC.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: PVWatts output 46,037-55,044 kWh/yr for the 41.7 kW array.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: C4 annual bill savings from solar about 9,207-13,211 USD/yr.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A (Efficiency only) cuts grid use 10.0-20.0 % of annual use = 33-67 % of the 30% goal; it does not reach the 30% goal at the low end.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A upfront cost 60,000-120,000 USD; net cost 60,000-120,000 USD (no incentive counted, see section 7); budget strain: within budget.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A simple payback 5.2-25.0 years on savings of 4,800-11,520 USD/yr. Simple payback, not the full SAM model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A outage backup 0.0-0.0 hours for critical loads. No battery, so solar shuts off in an outage.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B (Efficiency + solar within budget) cuts grid use 29.2-42.9 % of annual use = 97-143 % of the 30% goal; it does not reach the 30% goal at the low end.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B upfront cost 185,100-307,650 USD; net cost 185,100-307,650 USD (no incentive counted, see section 7); budget strain: within budget.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B simple payback 7.5-22.0 years on savings of 14,007-24,731 USD/yr. Simple payback, not the full SAM model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B outage backup 0.0-0.0 hours for critical loads. No battery, so solar shuts off in an outage.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C (Full path to the goal (deep efficiency + full solar + backup battery)) cuts grid use 34.2-47.9 % of annual use = 114-160 % of the 30% goal; it reaches the goal even at the low end.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C upfront cost 755,100-1,227,650 USD; net cost 755,100-1,227,650 USD (no incentive counted, see section 7); budget strain: over budget.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C simple payback 27.3-74.8 years on savings of 16,407-27,611 USD/yr. Simple payback, not the full SAM model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C outage backup 6.8-8.0 hours for critical loads.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Rooftop solar alone covers only 19.2-22.9% of annual use and does not reach the 30% goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Con Edison SC-9 Rate I, effective 2026-07-01, energy charge range. Confirm the tariff against a recent bill.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: DSIRE lists the NYSERDA Clean Energy Communities grant as open, but the official NYSERDA page says closed (retrieved 2026-10-10). DSIRE is only a finder, so the official closed status is used and the grant is left out of net cost.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Net cost counts no incentive: the saved incentive data is sample data (A5), so every program is left out until verified live. Costs use benchmark prices (A9).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: confirm the tariff against a recent bill and the budget year and type.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: structural PE/RA analysis and a roof condition survey before any solar design.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: LED lighting and controls first (Scenario A).
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and interconnection: licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review and the Con Edison interconnection application.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: the roof array sized in Scenario B once reviews pass.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: add storage if funding allows (Scenario C) and verify savings against bills.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario C battery of 800 kWh supports about 6.8-8.0 hours of the 100 kW critical load.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Battery sizing is sample REopt data, not a live optimization.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Scenarios A and B give no backup power: solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Licensed Professional Engineer or Registered Architect structural analysis for rooftop solar loads, as NYC DOB requires.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Roof condition survey by a qualified roofing contractor before design.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: NYC licensed electrician for interconnection and service upgrades.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: FDNY rooftop access review for equipment layout.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Con Edison utility interconnection review and application.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: Rooftop solar plus efficiency is unlikely to reach net-zero on this roof; plan off-site renewable procurement for the remainder.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Battery sizing, incentives, hazard ratings and the tariff are saved sample data, not live results; confirm them before committing funds.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Conflict: DSIRE (finder) says open, the official NYSERDA page says closed. The official status wins; the closed status was saved to the versioned cache from the official page, and nothing from DSIRE was saved.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Session intake, fictional building records, PVWatts, REopt, utility, incentive and hazard samples for case7_dsire_conflict, the internal calculate tool and the simple financial model.
claims.label: FACT
